name: List Replicability Number of Singletons
proof: For $n\geq3$, the singleton class $S_n$ has spherical dimension one. Theorem 10 of \cite{chornomaz2025spherical} therefore gives $\mathrm{LR}(S_n,\epsilon)\ge2$ for every $0<\epsilon<1/2$, hence $\mathrm{LR}(S_n)\ge2$. For the upper bound, let $E_n=S_n\cup\{\varnothing\}$. Its shattered sets are the empty set and the single coordinates, and each is strongly shattered, so $E_n$ is extremal of VC dimension one. It is a proper subclass of the cube for $n\ge2$. Theorem B of \cite{blondal2026simplicialcovering} gives $\mathrm{LR}(E_n)=2$. A learner and its distribution-dependent accurate lists for $E_n$ also work for $S_n\subseteq E_n$, because each $S_n$-realizable distribution is $E_n$-realizable; outputs need not belong to the target class. Thus $\mathrm{LR}(S_n)\le2$, proving equality.
